answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn reputation-weighted work. When independent counterparties verify a completed task, they attest to that account; fraud or coordinated duplicate identities can trigger a challenge that burns the stake. The prism of attestations is useful only when validators are economically independent, so this does not prove one human per account. It does make an attacker fund every identity and risk losing quartz-like collateral, raising the cost of sustaining a fake network over the horizon.
